figurative_meaning: Making a mountain out of a molehill; exaggerating a small issue.
example: Chinna godavani goranta daanni kondanta chesaru.

idiom: చెవిటి వాడి ముందు శంఖం ఊదినట్లు (Cheviti vaadi mundu shankham oodinatlu)
literal_meaning: Blowing a conch in front of a deaf person.
figurative_meaning: Wasting words on someone who refuses to listen or understand.
example: Vaadiki advice ivvadam cheviti vaadi mundu shankham oodinatlu.

idiom: గుడ్డి కన్నా మెల్ల మేలు (Guddi kanna mella melu)
literal_meaning: A squint is better than blindness.
figurative_meaning: Something is better than nothing.
example: Asalu job lekapovadam kante chinna job raavadam guddi kanna mella melu.

idiom: చంకలో పిల్లిని పెట్టుకొని ఊరంతా వెతికినట్లు (Chankalo pillini pettukoni oorantha vethikinatlu)
literal_meaning: Keeping a cat in the armpit and searching the whole town.
figurative_meaning: Searching everywhere for something that is right in front of you.
example: Pen chethilone pettukoni chankalo pillini pettukoni oorantha vethikinatlu vethukuthunnava?

idiom: పిల్లి కళ్ళు మూసుకుని పాలు తాగుతూ... (Pilli kallu musukuni paalu thaguthu...)
literal_meaning: A cat drinks milk with its eyes closed thinking no one sees.
figurative_meaning: Doing something wrong secretly, foolishly believing no one notices.
example: Nuvvu chese thappulu andarikii thelusu, pilli kallu musukuni paalu thaguthunnanukoku.

idiom: గురువింద గింజ తన నలుపు ఎరుగదు (Guruvinda ginja thana nalupu erugadu)
literal_meaning: The guruvinda seed doesn't know its own blackness.
figurative_meaning: A person ignoring their own faults while criticizing others.
example: Vaadu eppudu itarulanu vimarsisthadu, guruvinda ginja thana nalupu erugadu.

idiom: కూసే గాడిద మేసే గాడిదని చెడగొట్టినట్లు (Koose gaadida mese gaadidani chedagottinatlu)
literal_meaning: A braying donkey ruined the grazing donkey.
figurative_meaning: Bad company corrupts good character.
example: Vaadi thoti thirigi veedu kuda chedipoyadu, koose gaadida mese gaadidani chedagottinatlu.

idiom: తల ప్రాణం తోకకు వచ్చినట్లు (Thala pranam thokaku vachinatlu)
literal_meaning: Life coming from the head to the tail.
figurative_meaning: Facing extreme hardship or fear.
example: Aa project complete cheselopu thala pranam thokaku vachindi.

idiom: మింగ మెతుకు లేదు, మీసాలకు సంపెంగ నూనె (Minga methuku ledu, meesalaku sampenga nune)
literal_meaning: No grain to swallow, but jasmine oil for the mustache.
figurative_meaning: Showing off outwardly despite extreme inner poverty or lack of substance.
example: Pocket lo rupayi ledu gani branded battalu, minga methuku ledu meesalaku sampenga nune.

idiom: దొంగలు పడ్డ ఆరు నెలలకు కుక్కలు మొరిగినట్లు (Dongalu padda aaru nelalaku kukkalu moriginatlu)
literal_meaning: Dogs barking 6 months after the robbery.
figurative_meaning: Reacting far too late to a situation to be of any use.
example: Incident ayina chaala rojula tharvatha respond avvadam dongalu padda aaru nelalaku kukkalu moriginatlu.

idiom: నోరు మంచిదైతే ఊరు మంచిదవుతుంది (Noru manchidaite ooru manchidavutundi)
literal_meaning: If the mouth is good, the town is good.
figurative_meaning: If you speak politely, everyone will be good to you.
example: Andarito kalupugoluga undu, noru manchidaite ooru manchidavutundi.

idiom: ఆవు చేలో మేస్తే దూడ గట్టున మేస్తుందా (Aavu chelo meste, duda gattuna mestunda)
literal_meaning: If the cow grazes in the field, will the calf graze on the edge?
figurative_meaning: Like father, like son; children imitate their parents.
example: Thandri dongathananalu chestunte koduku kooda alage untadu, aavu chelo meste duda gattuna mestunda.

idiom: కుడితిలో పడ్డ ఎలుక లాగా (Kuditilo padda eluka laaga)
literal_meaning: Like a rat fallen in rice wash.
figurative_meaning: Being stuck in a messy dilemma unable to get out.
example: Rendu offers vachi etu vellalo theliyaka kuditilo padda eluka laaga unnadu.

literal_meaning: I gave the betel leaves, now fight to death.
figurative_meaning: Washing one's hands of all responsibility and letting others deal with the mess.
example: Nenu rules cheppesanu, thamboolalichhesanu thannuku chavandi.

literal_meaning: The fence grazing the crop.
figurative_meaning: The protector turning into the predator.
example: Police ye donga ayithe kanche chenu mesinatlu.

idiom: అత్త మీద కోపం దుత్త మీద చూపినట్లు (Attha meeda kopam duttha meeda chupinatlu)
literal_meaning: Showing anger towards the mother-in-law on the pot.
figurative_meaning: Displaced anger; taking out frustration on innocent people or objects.
example: Boss meeda kopam wife meeda chupinchadu, attha meeda kopam duttha meeda chupinatlu.

literal_meaning: Distant mountains are smooth.
figurative_meaning: The grass is always greener on the other side.
example: Vere desham vellali anukuntunnadu, doorapu kondalu nunupu kadha.

literal_meaning: Writings on water.
figurative_meaning: Something that is fleeting, impermanent, or useless.
example: Vaadi matalu neetilo raathalu, eppudu maripothadu.

idiom: కప్పకు పుండు వస్తే పాము తల దడిమినట్లు (Kappaku pundu vaste paamu thala dadiminatlu)
literal_meaning: Snake massaging a frog's wound.
figurative_meaning: Hypocritical help from an enemy who actually intends to harm you.
example: Vaadu saayam chestunnanu antunnadu jagratha, kappaku pundu vaste paamu thala dadiminatlu.

idiom: పెదవి దాటితే పెన్న దాటుతుంది (Pedavi daatithe penna daatuthundi)
literal_meaning: If it crosses the lip, it crosses the Penna river.
figurative_meaning: A secret once spoken spreads uncontrollably and widely.
example: Evarkii cheppaku, pedavi daatithe penna daatuthundi.

idiom: దీపం ఉండగానే ఇల్లు చక్కబెట్టుకోవాలి (Deepam undagane illu chakkabettukovali)
literal_meaning: Set the house in order while the lamp is burning.
figurative_meaning: Make hay while the sun shines; utilize opportunities while they last.
example: Vayasu unnapude sampaadinchukovali, deepam undagane illu chakkabettukovali.

literal_meaning: A new beggar doesn't know the time of day.
figurative_meaning: A novice lacks a sense of timing or etiquette in their new role.
example: Vaadiki job kothaga vachindi over chestunnadu, kottha bicchagadu podderagadu.

idiom: ఉరుము ఉరుమి మంగలం మీద పడ్డట్టు (Urumu urumi mangalam meeda paddattu)
literal_meaning: Thunder rolling and falling on the earthen pan.
figurative_meaning: A huge buildup that results in a minor or pathetic outcome.
example: Pedda meeting petti chivariki emi cheppaledu, urumu urumi mangalam meeda paddattu.

idiom: బొగ్గులు కడిగితే పాలు అవుతాయా (Boggulu kadigithe paalu avuthaya)
literal_meaning: If you wash coal, will it become milk?
figurative_meaning: You cannot change someone's inherent bad nature.
example: Vaadini entha marchalani chusina labham ledu, boggulu kadigithe paalu avuthaya?

idiom: తాడి చెట్టు ఎక్కే వాడిని ఎంత వరకు ఎగదోయాలి (Thaadi chettu ekke vaadini entha varaku egadoyali)
literal_meaning: How far can you push up someone climbing a palm tree?
figurative_meaning: You can only help someone so much; eventually, they must do the work themselves.
example: Nenu sagam saayam chesanu, thaadi chettu ekke vaadini entha varaku egadoyali?

idiom: శివుని ఆజ్ఞ లేనిదే చీమైనా కుట్టదు (Shivuni aagna lenide cheemaina kuttadu)
literal_meaning: Even an ant won't bite without Lord Shiva's command.
figurative_meaning: Everything happens according to the will of God.
example: Manam entha badhapaddina jarigede jaruguthundi, shivuni aagna lenide cheemaina kuttadu.

idiom: తన కోపమే తన శత్రువు (Thana kopame thana shatruvu)
literal_meaning: One's anger is one's enemy.
figurative_meaning: Anger only destroys the person who is angry.
example: Kopam tagginchuko, thana kopame thana shatruvu.

idiom: పాము చావకూడదు, కర్ర విరగకూడదు (Paamu chavakudadu, karra viragakudadu)
literal_meaning: The snake shouldn't die, the stick shouldn't break.
figurative_meaning: Resolving a conflict safely without causing harm to either side.
example: Godava peddadavvakunda paamu chavakudadu karra viragakudadu anattu problem solve chey.

idiom: పేరు గొప్ప ఊరు దిబ్బ (Peru goppa ooru dibba)
literal_meaning: Great name, but the town is a dump.
figurative_meaning: Famous in name but lacking in actual substance.
example: Aa college peru matrame goppa, lopala emi ledu, peru goppa ooru dibba.

idiom: మూలిగే నక్క మీద తాటికాయ పడ్డట్టు (Moolige nakka meeda thaatikaya paddattu)
literal_meaning: A palm fruit falling on a groaning fox.
figurative_meaning: A sudden disaster striking someone already suffering.
example: Appultho unna vaadiki accident ayindi, moolige nakka meeda thaatikaya paddattu.

idiom: రాత్రి అయితే గానీ రంగులు తెలియవు (Rathri ayithe gaani rangulu theliyavu)
literal_meaning: Colors aren't known until night falls.
figurative_meaning: True colors or difficulties are only revealed during tough times.
example: Kastam vasthene evaru elantivaro thelustundi, rathri ayithe gaani rangulu theliyavu.

literal_meaning: A cotton wick becoming a nail.
figurative_meaning: Something insignificant becoming a huge nuisance or threat over time.
example: Chinna appu eku mekai kurchundi.

literal_meaning: Doing harm to the benefactor.
figurative_meaning: Biting the hand that feeds you.
example: Ninnu nammina vaarini mosam cheyaku, upakariki apakaram cheyadam papam.

literal_meaning: Wind joining the fire.
figurative_meaning: A bad situation becoming worse due to an external factor.
example: Vaadi kopaniki nee maatalu agniki vayuvu thodainatlu ayyayi.

literal_meaning: A cat standing as witness for a rat.
figurative_meaning: An untrustworthy or compromised witness; a conflict of interest.
example: Donga ki inko donga support cheyadam elukaku pilli sakshi lanti de.

literal_meaning: Find the joint and apply the brand.
figurative_meaning: Speak or act precisely where it hurts or matters the most.
example: Vaadi weakness thelusukuni keelerigi vatha pettadu.

idiom: గొంగళిలో తింటూ వెంట్రుకలు ఏరుకున్నట్లు (Gongalilo thintu ventrukalu eerukunnatlu)
literal_meaning: Eating from a wool blanket and picking out hairs.
figurative_meaning: Complaining about inevitable minor flaws in a situation.
example: Chinna thappulanu pattinchukoku, gongalilo thintu ventrukalu eerukunnatlu avuthundi.

idiom: గుడ్డి ఎద్దు జొన్న చేలో పడ్డట్టు (Guddi eddu jonna chelo paddattu)
literal_meaning: A blind ox falling into a cornfield.
figurative_meaning: Doing things haphazardly and blindly ruining everything without direction.
example: Vaadiki em theliyakunda paninatha paduchesadu, guddi eddu jonna chelo paddattu.

idiom: తీయగా తీయగా రాగం, మూలగగా మూలగగా రోగం (Theeyaga theeyaga raagam, moolagaga moolagaga rogam)
literal_meaning: Singing makes a tune sweet, groaning makes sickness worse.
figurative_meaning: Practice makes perfect, but constant complaining breeds negativity.
example: Eppudu edavaku, theeyaga theeyaga raagam moolagaga moolagaga rogam.

literal_meaning: Unable to swallow, unable to vomit.
figurative_meaning: Being caught in an extremely difficult dilemma.
example: Aa kothha rules tho staff mingaleeka kakkaleeka avastha paduthunnaru.

idiom: ముందొచ్చిన చెవుల కన్నా వెనకొచ్చిన కొమ్ములు వాడి (Mundochina chevula kanna venakochina kommulu vaadi)
literal_meaning: Horns that came later are sharper than the ears that came first.
figurative_meaning: Newcomers or juniors outshining the seniors.
example: Kothaga vachina kurradu senior kante baaga chestunnadu, mundochina chevula kanna venakochina kommulu vaadi.

idiom: రొంపిలో పడ్డ పంది లాగా (Rompilo padda pandi laaga)
literal_meaning: Like a pig stuck in mud.
figurative_meaning: A person who is stuck in a messy situation and cannot escape.
example: Appula baadhaltho rompilo padda pandi laaga thayarayyadu.

idiom: పుండు మీద కారం చల్లినట్లు (Pundu meeda kaaram challinatlu)
literal_meaning: Sprinkling chili powder on a wound.
figurative_meaning: Adding insult to injury.
example: Akkade badhalo unte nuvvu velli inka edipinchadam pundu meeda kaaram challinatlu.

idiom: ఆకలి రుచి ఎరుగదు, నిద్ర సుఖమెరుగదు (Aakali ruchi erugadu, nidra sukhamerugadu)
literal_meaning: Hunger knows no taste, sleep knows no comfort.
figurative_meaning: When completely exhausted or starving, quality doesn't matter.
example: Rendu rojulu nunchi nidra ledu, aakali ruchi erugadu nidra sukhamerugadu.

literal_meaning: Like a cow studying grammar.
figurative_meaning: Doing something completely out of one's depth or comprehension.
example: Vaadiki science theliyadu, technical ga matladatam aavu vyakaranam chadinatlu.

idiom: ఉన్న మాట చెబితే ఉలుకెక్కువ (Unna maata chebithe ulukekkuva)
literal_meaning: Speaking the truth causes more irritation.
figurative_meaning: People get angry when confronted with the bitter truth.
example: Nenu nijam chebithe neeku kopam enduku, unna maata chebithe ulukekkuva.

idiom: ఎక్కడ వేసిన గొంగళి అక్కడే ఉన్నట్లు (Ekkada vesina gongali akkade unnatlu)
literal_meaning: The blanket remaining exactly where it was thrown.
figurative_meaning: Zero progress made in a task over a long period of time.
example: One year nunchi work chestunnam gani ekkada vesina gongali akkade unnatlu undi.

idiom: ఏరు దాటాక బోడి మల్లన్న (Eru daataka bodi mallanna)
literal_meaning: Calling the boatman 'bald Mallanna' after crossing the river.
figurative_meaning: Being extremely ungrateful once a favor is received.
example: Sahayam theesukoni ippudu nannu thidutunnava, eru daataka bodi mallanna.

idiom: కడుపు చించుకుంటే కాళ్ళ మీద పడుతుంది (Kadupu chinchukunte kalla meeda paduthundi)
literal_meaning: Tearing your own stomach drops things on your feet.
figurative_meaning: Washing dirty linen in public only brings shame to your own family.
example: Family godavalu bayata cheppaku, kadupu chinchukunte kalla meeda paduthundi.

idiom: కుక్కను తెచ్చి సింహాసనం మీద కూర్చోబెట్టినట్లు (Kukkanu thechi simhasanam meeda kurchobettinatlu)
literal_meaning: Bringing a dog and making it sit on a throne.
figurative_meaning: Elevating an undeserving, ill-mannered person to a high position.
example: Vaadiki promotion ivvadam kukkanu thechi simhasanam meeda kurchobettinatlu.

idiom: కూటికి గతి లేదు, కులమెక్కువ (Kootiki gathi ledu, kulamekkuva)
literal_meaning: No food to eat, but boastful of high caste.
figurative_meaning: Having no actual wealth or success, but showing off false pride.
example: Appulu chesi karchu chestunnadu, kootiki gathi ledu kulamekkuva.

idiom: గుడిని, గుడిలో లింగాన్ని మింగే రకం (Gudini, gudilo linganni minge rakam)
literal_meaning: The type to swallow the temple and the idol inside.
figurative_meaning: An extremely corrupt and greedy person.
example: Aa politician ni nammaku, gudini gudilo linganni minge rakam.

idiom: చెట్టు పేరు చెప్పి కాయలు అమ్మినట్లు (Chettu peru cheppi kayalu amminatlu)
literal_meaning: Selling fruits by taking the name of the tree.
figurative_meaning: Using someone else's famous name or brand to benefit yourself.
example: Vaadu nanna peru cheppukoni brathukestunnadu, chettu peru cheppi kayalu amminatlu.

literal_meaning: No bone in the hand.
figurative_meaning: Being extremely generous and giving freely.
example: Aayana dhanam ivvadamlo chethiki emuka ledu.

idiom: తడి గుడ్డతో గొంతు కోయడం (Thadi guddatho gonthu koyadam)
literal_meaning: Cutting a throat with a wet cloth.
figurative_meaning: Betraying someone slowly and sweetly from the inside.
example: Nuvvu friend ani nammithe thadi guddatho gonthu kosavu.

idiom: తలలు బోడులైనా తలపులు బోడులా (Thalalu bodulaina thalapulu bodulaa)
literal_meaning: Even if heads are bald, are thoughts bald?
figurative_meaning: Outward simplicity doesn't mean a lack of intelligence or complex thoughts.
example: Sanyasi ani theesipareyaku, thalalu bodulaina thalapulu bodulaa.

idiom: తాడెత్తు ఎదిగినా బుద్ధెత్తు లేదు (Thaadetthu edigina buddhetthu ledu)
literal_meaning: Grew as tall as a palm tree but no brain at all.
figurative_meaning: Physical growth without corresponding mental maturity.
example: Entha peddavadaivyo gani thaadetthu edigina buddhetthu ledu.

idiom: నక్క ఎక్కడ, నాగలోకం ఎక్కడ (Nakka ekkada, nagalokam ekkada)
literal_meaning: Where is the fox, and where is heaven?
figurative_meaning: A mismatch of monumental proportions; comparing the lowest to the highest.
example: Vaaditho nannu compare cheyaku, nakka ekkada nagalokam ekkada.

idiom: నీటిలో మొసలి ఏనుగును పట్టుకుంటుంది (Neetilo mosali enugunu pattukuntundi)
literal_meaning: In water, a crocodile can catch an elephant.
figurative_meaning: Everyone is powerful on their home turf.
example: Vaadi area lo vaade king, neetilo mosali enugunu pattukuntundi kadha.

idiom: నోటితో నవ్వి నొసటితో వెక్కిరించినట్లు (Notitho navvi nosatitho vekkirinchinatlu)
literal_meaning: Smiling with the mouth, mocking with the forehead.
figurative_meaning: Being two-faced or hypocritical.
example: Vaadu bayataki friend kani notitho navvi nosatitho vekkirinchinatlu chestadu.

literal_meaning: The son of a scholar is a dunce.
figurative_meaning: Genius is not always inherited.
example: Aayana entho goppa scientist kani vaadi koduku pandita putra shuntha.

idiom: పాలు తాగి రొమ్ము గుద్దినట్లు (Paalu thaagi rommu gudhinatlu)
literal_meaning: Drinking milk and punching the breast.
figurative_meaning: Biting the hand that feeds you.
example: Company nunchi anni theesukoni vallane mosam chesadu, paalu thaagi rommu gudhinatlu.

idiom: పెళ్లికి వెళ్తూ పిల్లిని చంకలో పెట్టుకెళ్ళినట్లు (Pelliki velthu pillini chankalo pettukellinatlu)
literal_meaning: Carrying a cat in the armpit while going to a wedding.
figurative_meaning: Carrying unnecessary trouble to an auspicious or good event.
example: Akkada antha manchiga jaruguthunte ee issue thesthaventi, pelliki velthu pillini chankalo pettukellinatlu.

idiom: మసి పూసి మారేడు కాయ చేసినట్లు (Masi poosi maredu kaya chesinatlu)
literal_meaning: Smearing ash and passing it off as a bael fruit.
figurative_meaning: Creating a fraudulent disguise or deceiving cleverly.
example: Pazhaya bandi ki masi poosi maredu kaya chesinatlu ammesadu.

idiom: రాజు తలుచుకుంటే దెబ్బలకు కొదవా (Raju thaluchukunte debbalaku kodavaa)
literal_meaning: If the king wills it, is there a shortage of beatings?
figurative_meaning: Absolute power dictates consequences effortlessly.
example: Boss anukunte nuvvu fire avvadaniki entha sepu, raju thaluchukunte debbalaku kodavaa.

literal_meaning: Like a wooden pestle sprouting leaves.
figurative_meaning: An absolutely impossible event.
example: Vaadu exam pass ayyada? Rokaliki chiguru puttinatlu undi.

idiom: వయసొస్తే వంకర కర్ర కూడా అందంగా ఉంటుంది (Vayasoste vankara karra kuda andanga untundi)
literal_meaning: In youth, even a crooked stick looks beautiful.
figurative_meaning: Youth imparts an automatic illusion of beauty.
example: Pellidu vachaka evaraina andanga kanipistharu, vayasoste vankara karra kuda andanga untundi.

idiom: వినేవాడు వెర్రివాడైతే, చెప్పేవాడు శివతత్వం చెప్పాడట (Vinevaadu verrivaadaithe, cheppevaadu shivatathvam cheppadata)
literal_meaning: If the listener is a fool, the speaker claims to speak divine philosophy.
figurative_meaning: Exploiting the ignorance of the audience with grand lies.
example: Vaadu cheppevaanni nammuthunnaru, vinevaadu verrivaadaithe cheppevaadu shivatathvam cheppadata.

idiom: శనగలు తింటూ శంఖం ఊదినట్లు (Sanagalu thintu shankham oodinatlu)
literal_meaning: Eating chickpeas while blowing a conch.
figurative_meaning: Trying to do two incompatible things at once and failing at both.
example: Rendu full-time jobs okesari cheyalem, sanagalu thintu shankham oodinatlu avuthundi.

idiom: సగం చదువు, సగం వైద్యం ప్రమాదకరం (Sagam chaduvu, sagam vaidyam pramadaakaram)
literal_meaning: Half knowledge and half medicine are dangerous.
figurative_meaning: Incomplete knowledge is worse than total ignorance.
example: Sagam thelusukoni expert laga matladaku, sagam chaduvu sagam vaidyam pramadaakaram.

idiom: సూది కోసం సోమవారం, దారం కోసం మంగళవారం (Soodi kosam somavaram, daaram kosam mangalavaram)
literal_meaning: Monday for a needle, Tuesday for thread.
figurative_meaning: Extreme laziness or procrastination.
example: Oka chinna pani cheyadaniki intha thiruguthunnava, soodi kosam somavaram daaram kosam mangalavaram laaga.

idiom: హంస నడక రాక, తన నడక మర్చిపోయినట్లు (Hamsa nadaka raaka, thana nadaka marchipoyinatlu)
literal_meaning: Failing to learn the swan's walk, and forgetting one's own.
figurative_meaning: Losing your originality while trying to imitate someone else.
example: English accent try chesi sontha bhasha marchipoyadu, hamsa nadaka raaka thana nadaka marchipoyinatlu.

idiom: చేతిలో చిల్లిగవ్వ లేదు, చంకలో జమిందారీ (Chethilo chilligavva ledu, chankalo jamindaari)
literal_meaning: Not a penny in hand, but the attitude of a landlord.
figurative_meaning: Being broke but putting on wealthy airs.
example: Bike ki petrol ledu gani Apple watch kavali, chethilo chilligavva ledu chankalo jamindaari.

literal_meaning: Giving a coconut to a monkey.
figurative_meaning: Giving something valuable to someone who doesn't know how to use it.
example: Vaadiki kothha phone isthe break chesadu, kothiki kobbarikaya ichinatlu.

literal_meaning: The past is past.
figurative_meaning: Let bygones be bygones; don't dwell on the past.
example: Jarigindedo jarigipoyindi, gatham gathaha anukoni munduku vellu.

idiom: ముందు నుయ్యి, వెనుక గొయ్యి (Mundu nuyyi, venuka goyyi)
literal_meaning: A well in front, a ditch behind.
figurative_meaning: Caught between the devil and the deep blue sea.
example: Ippudu job quit cheyalenu, ala ani continue avvalenu, mundu nuyyi venuka goyyi la undi.
